item.title: At least 40 rescued, 2 dead as boat capsizes after machete fight near Puerto Rico
item.description: A machete fight aboard a makeshift migrant boat near Mona Island caused it to capsize, leaving survivors stranded in open waters for over 12 hours.
item.content:encoded:
At least 40 people were rescued in open waters by the U.S. Coast Guard and two people died after their boat capsized several miles from a tiny, uninhabited island west of Puerto Rico following a fight that involved a machete, officials said on Monday.

Survivors said there was an estimated 60 people aboard, according to the Coast Guard.

The Coast Guard said the makeshift boat capsized late Sunday after a fight in which some people were severely injured by a machete, forcing the group to jump into the water despite not wearing life vests.

Survivors had spent more than 12 hours in the water when someone on a boat passing near Mona Island noticed them at around noon on Monday.

CBP, COAST GUARD INTERCEPT MIGRANT VESSEL HEADING FOR PUERTO RICO; 40 APPREHENDED INCLUDING UZBEK NATIONAL

The person alerted authorities and helped rescue four people at that moment.

Rescue efforts were still ongoing as of Monday evening.

The Coast Guard said it was not immediately known where the people who were on the capsized boat were from.

Migrants fleeing poverty and violence have long traveled from Hispaniola, the island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, to Puerto Rico and other islands, moving through the Mona Passage.

Many of these migrants navigate the passage on makeshift boats that can capsize in treacherous waters.

This incident marked only the latest deadly voyage.

In June 2022, 11 Haitian women and girls were buried in Puerto Rico after their grossly overloaded boat capsized in open waters northwest of the U.S. territory.

COAST GUARD OPENS FIRE ON BOAT SMUGGLING 25 CHINESE NATIONALS NEAR FLORIDA AFTER IT REFUSED TO STOP

Last week, police in the Turks and Caicos Islands detained a makeshift vessel carrying 60 Haitian migrants.

In June, 240 Haitian migrants were detained near the the Turks and Caicos Islands.

Gang violence has displaced a record 1.5 million people across Haiti, where more than 3,000 people were reportedly killed between January and June, according to U.N. data.

Armed men control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince and portions of land in Haiti’s central region and beyond.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: State Department considers sharing passport records for voter citizenship checks
item.description: The State Department is assessing how to share passport records with state and local officials to verify citizenship on voter registration rolls.
item.content:encoded:
The State Department is assessing how it could grant state and local officials access to federal passport records to verify voters' citizenship status ahead of the midterm elections in November.

The department is weighing how to share passport information with state and local officials, as well as some nonprofit groups, as part of the initiative that aims to ensure registered voters are U.S. citizens.

The objective of the plan is to share the information in a way that "protects Americans' data, deters fraud and supports the integrity of U.S. citizenship," a department spokesperson said in a statement to NewsNation.

The Justice Department disclosed the plan in a court filing last week, saying federal officials plan to use passport records to identify potential noncitizens on voter registration rolls.

TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN IN ELECTION INTEGRITY FIGHT AS STATES GAIN NEW VOTER ROLL TOOL

According to the filing, the State Department will publish a notice in the Federal Register proposing to share information contained in the Passport Services Records system with other federal agencies.

The notice would permit "information sharing with various entities utilizing federal government verification platforms, for the purpose of verifying the identity or citizenship for users accessing government websites and applications, voter eligibility, and other governmental services," according to the filing.

The records the Trump administration plans to share include personally identifiable information contained in the State Department's Passport Services Records system.

The 1974 Privacy Act requires the federal government to provide public notice establishing a new "routine use" for records maintained in a federal records system.

The DOJ filing said the notice could be published in the Federal Register as early as Oct. 22.

The filing came just days before a 6-3 Supreme Court decision on Friday that allowed the Department of Homeland Security to share citizenship information so local governments can verify whether registered voters are U.S. citizens.

DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED

Earlier attempts by the administration to use federal records to verify voter eligibility primarily relied on records from the Social Security Administration and DHS, with several of those efforts halted by successful court challenges.

The filing was submitted in a lawsuit brought by the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee against President Trump over his executive order on mail voting. The Supreme Court recently blocked the U.S. Postal Service from implementing parts of that order, though other provisions remain in effect.

The filing was submitted in a case brought by the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee and other Democratic plaintiffs challenging Trump’s executive order on mail voting. The Supreme Court recently declined to lift a lower-court injunction blocking the U.S. Postal Service from adopting its final mail-ballot rule for the November elections.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's push to probe holdout juror hits snag before pivotal retrial hearing
item.description: Lindsay Clancy returns to court in person as her defense pushes a double jeopardy motion and seeks to investigate holdout juror Michael Desronvil.
item.content:encoded:
PLYMOUTH, Mass. — A Massachusetts judge overseeing the Lindsay Clancy case is expected to hear arguments on her double jeopardy motion Tuesday, while another push to investigate the lone holdout juror in her mistrial may be on hold — for now.

Clancy is expected in court in person for the first time since her trial ended in a deadlocked jury and the judge declared a mistrial on Sept. 4.

In the weeks since her mistrial, Clancy's case has remained a topic of national interest, with fellow jurors and Clancy's defense attorney attacking the lone holdout. At the same time, Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz's office has been relatively quiet about their plans for a potential retrial.

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR ASKS FOR ONE THING IN NEW VIDEO AFTER MISTRIAL DRAMA

LINDSAY CLANCY'S PUSH TO INVESTIGATE HOLDOUT JUROR COULD BE PAUSED AS DEFENSE, PROSECUTORS AGREE TO ADJOURN

Here's a roundup of what to expect as she returns to court:

Clancy's defense lawyer Kevin Reddington had called for an inquiry into the lone holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, whom he has dubbed "the obstructionist juror." Desronvil opposed 11 others on the panel and was the only one who wanted to find her guilty until the end.

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR'S LAWYER TORCHES 'LOONEY TUNES MOTION' TO INVESTIGATE HIM

However, according to Desronvil's attorney, Edward Paltzik, both Reddington and Plymouth County prosecutors agreed to adjourn that motion after counsel for the holdout raised an objection because they didn't yet have access to impounded materials necessary to file a response.

"The DA and Reddington consent to adjourn the motion to investigate Michael," Paltzik told Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany Monday.

ATTORNEY FOR LONE HOLDOUT JUROR IN LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL PUSHES BACK ON CLAIMS OF REFUSING THE LAW

"If Judge Sullivan signs an order today, much of it could be adjourned," he said. "Either way, a status conference is still likely."

Reddington pushed back, forcefully, while conceding that he and the district attorney's office had agreed to continue the motion out of professional courtesy to local counsel now representing the juror.

LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON FIRES BACK AT LONE HOLDOUT JUROR'S ATTORNEY AFTER FIERY INTERVIEW

"Earlier today, both the government and I were contacted by a professional local attorney who represents Juror Doe," he said, not using the juror's name due to an impoundment order from the court. "That attorney requested — as any qualified counsel would — adequate time to review our motion and reply."

He added, "As is professional courtesy, both the government and I agreed to continue this specific motion to a later date at their request. The motion remains active, fully alive, and is currently pending a ruling from Judge Sullivan. We will not allow a publicity-seeking opportunist to twist simple courtroom courtesy into a victory that does not exist."

The terms adjourned and continued are similar but have distinct meanings.

"Adjournment generally signifies that something like a hearing is off indefinitely especially because no date is specified," explained retired Massachusetts Judge Carol Erskine. "A continuance is a simple request by a party or two parties to get a new date. [Reddington] objects because adjournment is a misrepresentation of what is happening."

CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE’S ‘DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD’: ATTORNEY

If Reddington ultimately prevails, the court could hold a Fidler hearing, where the judge would question Desronvil.

"There are three phases to a hearing like that," said Erskine, who is also a child welfare advocate and has been closely following the case. "This is something that could result in a strong manifest necessity claim but hard to tell until it happens."

LINDSAY CLANCY'S ATTORNEY ASKS JUDGE TO ACQUIT HER OUTRIGHT, ENDING CASE AND BARRING A RETRIAL

Manifest necessity is the legal standard required to hold a second trial. Erskine said the motion is a long-shot but Reddington is likely laying the foundation for an appeal in the future.

"The big issue, in my opinion, is whether outside information came into the jury room and whether a judge can find that any 'hypothetical juror' would let it influence his decision," she told Fox News Digital. "It’s definitely more complicated than that, but there is case law about it."

"This is a strange new world in which disagreeing jurors and their surrogates conduct a public debate after the trial in the media and social media," said Jack Lu, another retired Massachusetts judge.

Reddington's request for an inquiry into Desronvil is largely based on allegations from other jurors who accused him of having reasonable doubt about the case and ignoring it. He is seeking phone records, his confidential juror questionnaire and police records.

However, he's also called him an "obstructionist" outside the courtroom and accused him of having an "agenda."

"[The other jurors] know that they were robbed — by one man — for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful and listened to this evidence," he told reporters after leaving the courthouse on Sept. 4, the day the mistrial was declared. 

Still, he downplayed speculation from legal analysts about a potential defamation lawsuit from the holdout against Clancy's team.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"Defamation law is textbook complex," he told Fox News Digital. "Statements made in court proceedings are privileged."

Statements made out of court that could appear to be "false statements of fact" may end up being considered opinions, he added.

"If a person says X happened, and we all know that person was not present, then it may be deemed to be an opinion," he said. "This might apply to any alleged statements about what happened in the jury room."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"I don’t think any of the legal maneuvering, double jeopardy, all that stuff, a hearing in the trial court with the juror, I don't think it’s going anywhere," said Mark Bederow, a New York-based criminal defense attorney and former prosecutor who is following the case.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

"If you get down to brass tacks, once you get through all this, now you have to look at the DA and say, what are you doing?" he added.

Most prosecutors would not seek a second trial in a case where only one juror agreed with them, he said, but that appears unlikely in this case.

GOT A TIP?

"At the first trial, the prosecution, in my view, failed miserably to satisfy their burden — but there is a credible argument that she's guilty and intended to cause their deaths and knew right from wrong," he said. "In order for them to win, they need to get better experts."

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The Commonwealth needs experts who can discredit Clancy's defense experts, he said. And prosecutors also have room to improve their jury selection.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

As for Reddington, he described him as "a titan of the Massachusetts bar" who is filing motions that make sense for his client's benefit, regardless of his commentary outside the courtroom.

"That's not frivolous, and any lawyer knows that," he told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Case Keenum's performance in win over Eagles should tell Bears this: Don't rush back Caleb Williams
item.description: Case Keenum finished 24-of-34 with two passing touchdowns and a rushing score, raising a key question about Caleb Williams' return timeline.
item.content:encoded:
Case Keenum turned back the clock, as the 38-year-old quarterback led the Chicago Bears to a resounding 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

It was Keenum’s first start since Week 16 of the 2023 season, but you wouldn’t have guessed that with how well he executed head coach Ben Johnson’s offense on his way to a performance to remember with his family and the rest of the NFL looking on.

Keenum’s performance was so good that the Bears need to be told one thing (if they weren’t thinking so already): don’t rush back Caleb Williams.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Yes, the franchise quarterback who is the Bears’ best chance to reach the Super Bowl – don’t rush him back onto the field.

Of course, this is only one performance from Keenum, who is the third-string quarterback on the Bears’ depth chart. Tyson Bagent is Williams’ usual backup, while the journeyman Keenum rounds out the depth in the room.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

However, Johnson stuck with Keenum as his starter this week in a key primetime matchup against the 2-0 Eagles, another team that is a strong candidate to come out of the NFC and make it back to the "Big Game." Bagent was cleared from concussion protocol, but he was Keenum’s backup heading into the night.

That’s how confident Johnson and the Bears were that Keenum would be able to execute the gameplan and get Chicago back on the winning track.

"Whatever happens today, I’m going to give God the glory. And hopefully it makes those kids proud," Keenum told ESPN before the game, pointing to his kids on the field prior to kickoff.

Johnson immediately started the game for Keenum with a few short passes to get his bearings, but it was clear from the opening drive that he was ready to do more than just dink and dunk his way to a win. Keenum led an 11-play drive that ended with Luther Burden III’s first touchdown catch of the season in a game that got him back on track after being quiet the first two weeks.

From there, Keenum continued to shine with well-timed passes, hitting his receivers in stride out of breaks. He was making the right pre-snap checks at the line of scrimmage, and he even made throws across the field with pressure right in his grill from the Eagles’ defense.

This wasn’t a game where Johnson tried to be extremely creative with the run game, getting D’Andre Swift and others involved to alleviate the pressure on Keenum. It was business as usual, it seemed, and it worked to hand Nick Sirianni and the Eagles their first loss of the season.

Keenum finished the game an efficient 24-of-34 for 247 yards with two touchdowns through the air, and oh yeah, his first rushing touchdown since 2019. It was the game-sealing score, as Keenum’s quarterback sneak was the last thing the Eagles thought would be coming on third-and-goal, and he dove across the goal line with a bear-sized smile on his face with his teammates celebrating around him.

This game was also further proof that Johnson remains arguably the best offensive mind in football, someone who can make anyone look good under center. But Keenum still had to execute his coach's wizardry, and he proved to be a viable option to hold down the fort and keep the offense moving while Williams recovers. With Williams dealing with an injury that’s always tricky for players in this league, there’s no reason to rush him back and risk aggravating it again.

The Bears seem to be in good hands with their 38-year-old journeyman at the helm, as they head into a matchup with the New York Jets at home in Week 4.

As for the Eagles, Jalen Hurts went 16-for-25 for 153 yards with a rushing touchdown and one interception thrown. It wasn’t a night to remember for either side of the ball, but they will need to get things going next week against the 1-2 Los Angeles Rams.

item.title: LeBron James admits he nearly joined the Knicks before Jalen Brunson won the NBA title without him
item.description: LeBron James revealed he nearly signed with the New York Knicks but backed off after Jalen Brunson led them to a title without him in free agency.
item.content:encoded:
LeBron James took the mic at 76ers Media Day, sounding like classic LeBron.

After a summer of endless free agency rumors, opting out of his contract, and leaving his family on the West Coast to chase another ring in the East, he finally landed in Philadelphia.

Yet before taking a single shot in a Sixers uniform, he was already laying down excuses and tossing his new teammates under the bus.

"If we can do that, then we can be a great team," he said.

"If we don't do that, then we'll be like, 'Oh man, it was a great team on paper. We had a lot of great talent, and we lost in the second round.' I don't wanna do that. I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round, I know that for sure. So the work needs to be done, and I'm ready to put the work in."

Classic LeBron. If they win, he is the savior. If they lose, the team on paper simply did not put in the work.

Then came the best part.

LeBron admitted he nearly signed with the New York Knicks, but backed off after they won a championship without him, knowing fans would roast him online for pulling a Kevin Durant.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," LeBron said. "One of the best places I've ever played. I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it. Y'all wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all."

"But much respect to the Knicks, obviously," LeBron added. "An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out Jalen Brunson. I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at, and I'm looking forward to it."

He wanted to end the drought himself.

Once Jalen Brunson took care of business, LeBron bailed for Philly.

Dropping LeBron into that locker room immediately raised questions about who actually runs the show in Philadelphia. Asked on Monday who the "alpha" of the Sixers is, Jaylen Brown shut it down cold: "Next question."

THE 76ERS JUMP TO BETTING FAVORITE OUT EAST AFTER LEBRON JAMES TAKES HIS TALENTS TO PHILADELPHIA

Then came the pandering to the Philly crowds.

"They know ball," LeBron said. "And if you're not doing what you're supposed to do, they're going to let you hear it, and I'm excited about that."

Sure you are, LeBron.

As for how he fits alongside Embiid and Tyrese Maxey entering Season 24, LeBron had zero doubts about his remaining capability.

"The luxury of my game is that I can do everything," James declared. "Literally, I can do everything."

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team, and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey ..." LeBron added.

item.title: Senate passes Protect College Sports Act with decisive vote
item.description: The Protect College Sports Act, which would set national rules for NIL deals, the transfer portal and more, was passed by the Senate on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
The Senate has passed the Protect College Sports Act, establishing national rules for college athletics, which includes standards for Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) deals, athlete compensation, recruiting, eligibility, transferring and more.

The bill, led by Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., was passed by a vote of 77-22 on Monday night.

President Donald Trump has urged lawmakers to pass the bill, saying "we have to get that done" prior to Congress' summer recess.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I’m urging the House and the Senate to come together, bipartisan if possible and it looks like they have done, to send the bill to my desk and I will sign it," he said the night he hosted members of Team USA from the Winter Olympic and Paralympic Games, who performed well earlier this year. "I think we have no choice. We have to get that done. If we don’t, we’re very foolish. Nobody knows what will happen. We’re in Never-Never Land. We’re not going to let that be happening. We’re not going to let that happen to these great people and others."

The bill finally got pushed to the next phase earlier this month, giving the Senate the opportunity to advance the bipartisan bill. Now, the bill will go to the House of Representatives, and Trump may see it on his desk to sign into law if it goes through there.

RAND PAUL: POLITICIANS SHOULD STAY OUT OF COLLEGE SPORTS AND LET ATHLETES COMPETE FREELY

"I think most people acknowledge that the current landscape of college sports is a mess," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said ahead of the vote. "It needs to be addressed."

The Protect College Sports Act would provide the collegiate governing body with greater antitrust legal protections while also establishing a uniform framework for college athletics in terms of NIL compensation, the transfer portal and more.

Cruz was the one pitching the bill since the NCAA made its decision to allow student-athletes the opportunity to benefit financially while playing college sports. However, there were no boundaries, and despite the NCAA attempting to clean up after the landmark decision in 2021, its asked lawmakers to step in for help.

"Some have asked why should Congress get in the middle of this? The answer is simple: because Congress screwed it up in the first place," Cruz said during a news conference on Monday.

"It has been the federal antitrust laws applied in litigation after litigation after litigation that have had the effect of tearing down essentially all the rules," he continued. "So right now it is the Wild West."

The bill would broadly add restrictions to the transfer portal for athletes, while creating a uniform eligibility framework of five years. Recruiting and tampering guardrails would be established, where schools or agents will have to follow specified timeframes when they’re allowed to contact or recruit an athlete. Also, a federal standard for NIL rules and a revenue-sharing cap would be set if the bill were to be signed into law.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

There are opponents of the bill, however, including Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn. who said it would take away bargaining power from the athletes, while creating exemptions from antitrust law for schools.

"The ‘chaos’ is that (mostly Black) athletes now have bargaining power and White coaches and sports industry execs hate it," Murphy said on X earlier this month.

Finally, Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., alongside Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., filed an amendment to the bill in August aimed at preventing the bill from overriding state laws that bar biological men from competing in women’s sports. They wanted to close, what they viewed as, a loophole to undo laws in their states designed to keep biological males out of women’s sports.

Hawley said earlier this month he voted to advance the legislation after saying his concern was addressed and fixed within the bill to his satisfaction.

The House is under recess until after the midterm elections, meaning a potential vote on the bill to send it to Trump's desk would have to wait.

item.title: Kentucky trooper, father of 3, gunned down during traffic stop as suspect captured after manhunt
item.description: Hayden Phillips, a 30-year-old Kentucky state trooper, leaves behind a wife and three sons after being killed during a routine stop on Interstate 65.
item.content:encoded:
A routine traffic stop on a Kentucky interstate turned deadly Monday when a state trooper was gunned down, launching a statewide manhunt that ended with a suspect in custody.

Trooper Hayden Phillips, 30, was killed along Interstate 65 in Warren County. He leaves behind a wife and three young sons.

"He was senselessly murdered," U.S. Attorney Kyle Bumgarner said at a Monday night news conference. "We have a wife that expected her husband to come home. We have three little boys who don’t have a dad."

SUSPECTS AT LARGE AFTER TUCSON POLICE RECRUIT KILLED, PIMA COUNTY CORRECTIONS OFFICER WOUNDED IN SHOOTING

Phillips was a three-year veteran of Kentucky State Police, assigned to Post 3 in Bowling Green. He graduated from Cadet Class 103 and was known to fellow troopers as Unit 369.

"Because he served us, because he served our community, because he wanted to keep each of us safe," Bumgarner said. "He gave the ultimate sacrifice."

Kentucky State Police Commissioner Col. Phillip Burnett Jr. pledged to pursue justice for Phillips.

"We will seek justice for Hayden," Burnett said. "Let me repeat that, we will seek justice for Hayden. We will not rest until this happens."

JURY CONVICTS KEVIN SALAZAR IN EXECUTION-STYLE KILLING OF LA DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER

Burnett called Phillips’ death one of the most difficult moments the agency could endure.

"His dedication to duty and commitment to the Commonwealth will never be forgotten," Burnett said. "Our hearts break for Trooper Phillips’ family, loved ones, and fellow troopers as we grieve this tremendous loss."

State police initially announced a trooper-involved shooting on northbound I-65 near the 38-mile marker. They then asked the public to watch for a bluish-gray Honda Civic with an Alabama tag that had been present during the shooting. A Blue Alert identified Emonnie Branch as the wanted person.

Louisville Metro Police took Branch into custody, and state police canceled the alert. Burnett said Branch was being charged with the murder of a first responder. Bumgarner said Branch would be returned to Warren County to face state murder charges.

MAN WANTED IN DEPUTY AMBUSH CAUGHT AFTER WILDLIFE CAMERA SIGHTING AND MAJOR MANHUNT

"I want you to know I only mentioned his name one time," Burnett said of Branch, condemning what he called the suspect’s "cowardly actions."

Authorities have not said why Phillips stopped the vehicle or whether Branch had a prior criminal record.

"One of our own was gunned down and murdered on the side of the road," Bumgarner said. He pledged that the Justice Department would give Kentucky prosecutors and investigators "every tool" and "every bit of support" it could provide.

Burnett addressed Phillips’ family directly, promising that state police would stand beside them.

"You will not walk this path alone," he said.

"Rest Easy U/369. We have it from here," state police wrote in a tribute to Phillips.

AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND

Gov. Andy Beshear called Phillips a hero who dedicated himself to protecting Kentucky. He said the trooper was also "a devoted husband and loving father to three children."

"Let us wrap our arms around this family during this unimaginable time," the governor wrote.

Rep. Brett Guthrie, R-Ky., thanked law enforcement for its swift work and said Phillips’ wife, their three young children and his colleagues were in his prayers. Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., urged people to pray for Phillips’ family and fellow officers.

Rep. Morgan McGarvey, D-Ky., also offered prayers for Phillips’ family and said Kentucky would not forget his service.

"Alongside his fellow KSP troopers and all who knew and loved him, we will not forget his service to our commonwealth," McGarvey wrote.

Country singer Lee Greenwood mourned Phillips, writing that he and his wife, Kim, had learned of the trooper’s death and would "always stand with the men and women in blue."

item.title: Will the College Football Playoff selection committee's new rules make their rankings better?
item.description: The College Football Playoff committee is adding strength of conference as a new metric, but questions about transparency and bias remain unanswered.
item.content:encoded:
There's no question that the College Football Playoff selection committee has a difficult job. And one where it's virtually impossible to please all interested parties.

In the current format, just 12 college football teams reach the playoffs, which has become the ultimate sign of success or failure for a program's season. Coaching changes are decided based on playoff appearances. Conference bragging rights, both in the public discourse and in deliberations, are determined based on playoff appearances.

Given the competing priorities at play, there's little chance of keeping everyone happy. There will always be a 13th best team in the country. Or a Power 4 school that feels like they missed out to allow a Group of 6 school to reach the tournament. Conferences will advocate for more of their member teams to be included. Group of 6 schools will argue that they deserve to be included after a good season, even if their schedules can't match up to top teams.

FLORIDA GATORS, MISSISSIPPI STATE SOAR, USC TUMBLES IN LATEST INEXPLICABLE AP TOP 25 POLL

It's a guarantee that their choices will lead to disagreement, debate, and some level of unhappiness. Especially because the rankings are based on human evaluation, and humans make mistakes, are biased, or have their own individual priorities and valuations.

Which is what makes the opacity of the committee's process and evaluation tools so frustrating.

For years, committee members have spoken about how they incorporate strength of schedule and resume into their deliberations and their top 25 poll. But there's little transparency as to how they determine the strength of schedule and resume. It's nice to say it, it's another to show your work. Are they creating their own metrics based on wins and losses against, say, AP ranked teams? Or is it just eye test? Or do they use more advanced, computer-driven analytics? Who knows?

Well, the committee revealed recently that they're now adding another metric to help inform their discussions: strength of conference. Oh good, more metrics with little transparency that will lead to more debate and disagreement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Heather Dinich from ESPN reported that the committee would now incorporate this new metric to help separate teams within the league.

"The CFP selection committee will incorporate another data point in late November that helps determine the strength of each conference based on the schedule strength of each team in its league,' she posted on X. "It will help separate teams in the SAME LEAGUE with similar records based on the strength of their conference opponents. (Ex: PSU doesn’t play Oregon, Ohio State or IU) It will also help separate teams with comparable records in different conferences based on how tough their league opponents were."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Sure. Sounds reasonable enough. But what's it based on?

How are they evaluating which teams have faced the "strongest" conference opponents? Win-loss record? AP Top 25 poll appearances? Random eye test? Computer analytics? How do they determine how to separate teams with comparable records in different conferences?

Again, the questions that the committee wants answers to, evaluating different schedules and conferences, are all valuable and important debates. The issue is that there's no transparency on how they're going to do it.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Some fans look at wins and losses or head-to-head matchups. Some like to use "ranked wins" or ranked games, though those can often be misleading based on when those games happen. For example, Texas A&M counts as a ranked win for LSU, even though it's clear the Aggies are far from a top 25 team. Others like to use analytics-based systems that are more objective and less biased toward a specific school or conference.

That should be the preference; remove bias, evaluate teams objectively, combine metrics to find the "best" teams that fit the criteria and limit the amount of campaigning and importance of the typically awful AP Poll. That should be the goal. But will it be the outcome?

item.title: Caleb Williams, limited by a hamstring injury, seen casually pacing Bears sideline during national anthem
item.description: Caleb Williams was caught pacing the Bears sideline during the national anthem before Monday Night Football despite being out with a hamstring strain.
item.content:encoded:
There was a lot going on during the national anthem prior to the Monday Night Football game between the Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles , and the strangest part was how Caleb Williams handled the moment.

The Mariachi Herencia de México, a Mexican mariachi band, performed the "Star-Spangled Banner". And while the anthem played , the two teams' players, coaches and others stood along the sidelines.

But Williams was an exception.

CALEB WILLIAMS AVOIDS MAJOR HAMSTRING INJURY AS MRI REVEALS A STRAIN BUT NO TEAR AFTER VIKINGS GAME SCARE

While the anthem was playing, Williams was seen on the ESPN national broadcast pacing along the Bears sideline as if he had somewhere else important to get to.

Williams , in fact, didn't have anywhere important to go because he isn't playing in this game – or possibly in a couple of others – while he recovers from a hamstring strain suffered in last week's loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

And yet, the guy who cannot move well enough to play because a soft tissue injury is walking around during the national anthem.

Maybe Williams doesn't know or doesn't care, but this is a ceremonial no-no at best and disrespectful at worst.

The patriotic Code of Conduct for the national anthem is available online, through a government website.

It reads:

"During rendition of the national anthem when the flag is displayed, all present except those in uniform should stand at attention facing the flag with the right hand over the heart."

That, believe it or not, has been the code since 1942.

In 1976, the code was amended to insert the requirement that "during the rendition of the national anthem when the flag is displayed, all persons present except those in uniform should stand at attention, face the flag, and place the right hand over the heart and men with headdress should remove the headdress and hold it at the left shoulder, the hand being over the heart and when the flag is not displayed, those present should face the music and act in the same manner they would if the flag were displayed."

This is not debatable. It's the universal code of conduct for Americans.

Maybe Williams isn't aware. The educational system today is not renowned for teaching traditional American values and traditions any more, and Williams, 24, is a product of that system.

Or maybe Williams doesn't really like to be bothered by the traditions of the national anthem. He was seen last season trying to chat with a teammate on the sideline during the national anthem.

This is going to bother some people. More than a few reacted negatively on social media about the behavior.

Other people will simply shrug it off as an oversight or not worthy of attention.

But they're going to have to wait a while.

item.title: Reparations activist does not expect compensation from New York officials as action is delayed for years
item.description: The U.S. Freedmen Project said New York's reparations commission delay proves the system is designed to stall, not deliver, for descendants.
item.content:encoded:
A reparations activist with a grassroots organization called the U.S. Freedmen Project told Fox News Digital that their group expects no financial compensation from New York state officials after lawmakers quietly delayed a high-profile study into historic remedies.

"What the mainstream reparations movement is really about ... is spinning your wheels until [those] to whom the debt is owed tire out, give up, and give in," U.S. Freedmen Project President Devine Prince told Fox News Digital. "That's the only reason why you would pursue race-based policies within a system and within a country that has the 14th Amendment, which bans and prohibits race-based policies."

The U.S. Freedmen Project — a group of self-identified "Foundational Black Americans" — aims to educate the public on the legal and historical distinctions between African Americans who are direct descendants of enslaved people in the U.S. and immigrants from Africa or the Caribbean who arrived voluntarily in recent decades.

CHAOS ERUPTS AT NY REPARATIONS HEARING AS ‘FOUNDATIONAL’ BLACK AMERICANS CLASH WITH LEFT-LEANING GROUPS

Prince’s comments follow sharp backlash after state leaders extended the timeline for the New York State Community Commission on Reparations Remedies to issue its final report. A provision embedded in the recently passed state budget pushed the commission's deadline back two years — from 2027 to 2029 — nearly four years beyond its original 2025 deadline.

The New York Civil Liberties Union (NYCLU) publicly criticized the delay in June.

"The state’s decision to spend an additional three years before it takes any action to address these harms raises a lot of questions about when Black New Yorkers will receive reparations," said Chantelle Williams, assistant director of the NYCLU’s Racial Justice Center.

"Meanwhile, the impact of discrimination continues to harm Black individuals and communities across the state. This delay is not just a bureaucratic inconvenience. It is a disservice to those who have suffered the profound and lasting consequences of inequality," Williams added.

NEW YORK FAR-LEFT GROUP CLAIMS REPARATIONS 'OWED' AS BLACKS' MEDIAN WEALTH 'NEARLY 15 TIMES LESS' THAN WHITES

The nine-member state commission, established by legislation signed by Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul in late 2023, was tasked with examining the Empire State's historical ties to slavery, Jim Crow-era discrimination, and economic disparities like redlining. The panel was charged with delivering recommendations for potential state-level financial compensation and policy reforms.

The commission recently concluded a series of statewide public hearings, culminating in a May 30 forum in Harlem titled "From Extraction to Repair: Closing the Racial Wealth Gap."

However, state lawmakers opted to move back the commission's deadline. Assemblymember Michaelle C. Solages, D-N.Y., who sponsored the original legislation, acknowledged the extension was requested to navigate a shifting national legal environment. Solages cited conservative legal challenges targeting diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives and the broader erosion of race-conscious policies. 

The budget measure also included a provision shielding commissioners from personal legal liability if targeted by lawsuits over their findings.

Lineage advocates with the U.S. Freedmen Project, who attended the Harlem hearing, pushed back strongly against both the delay and the commission's framework. They argue that reparations should be strictly limited to direct descendants of individuals enslaved within the United States rather than broader race-based categories.

Activists with the group contend that progressive organizations like the NYCLU fail to represent the distinct legal and historical claims of descendant Black Americans by attempting to include recent Black immigrants under the same umbrella.

Prince claimed that members of the New York commission were appointed to preserve the status quo rather than deliver tangible results.

"These are individuals that have been put in place to keep the status quo intact while pretending they're working to undo it," Prince said. "There's a bunch of things moving around in the background that tie them to this ideology that benefits them if we keep the status quo of race-based advocacy alive."

"What we are focused on is true repair — and, unfortunately, true repair means repairing those who were truly harmed. Not everyone who comes in and says, 'Hey, I'm included in that, too,'" he added.

Supporters of the Freedmen Project maintain that any state-level reparations bill based on race rather than direct lineage would violate the U.S. Constitution's Equal Protection Clause. They urged state officials to adopt strict lineage-based criteria to reduce the program's exposure to legal challenges.

New York is part of a broader wave of blue states and municipalities attempting to construct local reparative frameworks. In Illinois, the Chicago suburb of Evanston, Illinois made headlines as the first U.S. city to distribute reparations, offering $25,000 housing grants to eligible Black residents.

Despite public hearings and ongoing research, Prince expressed skepticism that New York state will ever deliver payments to descendants.

TRUMP ADMIN VOWS TO STOP REPARATIONS PROGRAMS, ACCUSES OFFICIALS OF 'VIRTUE SIGNALING' TO GET 'VOTES'

"Realistically, I'm expecting the same thing that I expected going into this: nothing," Prince said. "Based on all the advocacy we did before this was even signed into law — all the recommendations we suggested and experts we brought to the New York Legislature to inform them on how to get this right — once all those things were ignored, I knew it would end up right where it is now. Realistically, I'm expecting them to find a way to distance themselves from this."

New York officials did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Did Cunningham buckle? Hell no. She doubled down with an Instagram post that declared she isn't backing down for anyone.

"I said what I said," she wrote.

This is the only way to do it. If there's one thing the mob hates more than anything, it's courage. You show it to them, they go away. It's just sad that so few seem to possess it.

NBC Sports football analyst Chris Simms was the latest to bow to online outrage over some perfectly reasonable comments. After Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was knocked out of Saturday's game due to a helmet-to-helmet hit by USC's Desman Stephens II, Simms did what an analyst is paid to do: analyze.

At halftime, Simms said that Moore's injury was a "Debbie Downer" moment because fans want to see teams at full strength. He then shared some advice his father told him about how to "make sure you get down in time and don't take any big hits." He added how Moore's late slide put Stephens in a "no-win situation."

DAN DAKICH CALLS CHRIS SIMMS' APOLOGY OVER DANTE MOORE SLIDE ANALYSIS 'SOFT A-- BULLS--T'

This is an ex-football player talking football. But apparently all Oregon fans wanted to hear was that this was the dirtiest hit in the history of the sport, so Sunday, Simms took to social media to write "I clearly did not show enough sympathy for the situation. I mishandled the situation and I was wrong. I'm sorry for that."

It seems like we see a new one of these every week. Earlier this month, Texas quarterback Arch Manning laughed at an AI meme of ESPN reporter Holly Rowe getting slapped by Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian. He was shamed into apologizing two days later. In July, Sandy Brondello, coach of the WNBA's Toronto Tempo, wanted a foul to be called on Atlanta's Angel Reese, and could be heard telling refs that Reese was a "protected species."

This is common lingo in Australia — Brondello's home country — where it's meant to express frustration over a player getting special treatment. But Brondello still issued a written apology to Reese, saying "I used a phrase that I shouldn't have used, and I take full responsibility for that."

And then, of course, there was Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown caving last year after doing the Trump dance after a touchdown in a game vs. Commanders. Said St. Brown: "First of all, if I offended anyone, I do apologize. I did not mean to offend anyone. It was just, we're having fun."

It's hard watching these sports figures shed their dignity with each one of these mea culpas. What they don't understand is that they are losing respect from the public every time they issue one. The outrage mob simply sees them as people who will fold the next time they want to sink their hooks into them. And the folks who would have supported them if they stood strong? They now see a spineless pushover.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This doesn't mean that people should never apologize. During his time in Seattle, Richard Sherman was infamous for his inability to ever take accountability for his wrongdoing. That's also a form of weakness — it's just wearing a different costume.

But to surrender when you've done nothing wrong? It's not noble, it's nauseating.

CHARLES BARKLEY DECLARES WNBA IS 'FOR WOMEN ONLY' AFTER ONGOING TRANSGENDER ATHLETE DEBATE

People like Cunningham know this. Charles Barkley, too. The Hall of Fame hooper is on record saying trans athletes don't belong in women's sports, and the blowback has been almost nonexistent because everyone knows he is going to hold firm in his position. That's the power of integrity.

The vocal minority shouldn't have the influence that it does. Yet it regularly turns titans of the sports world into mush. Don't be like Chris Simms, who gave into the mob. Be like Cunningham, who decided to stand up to it. Sophie's choice is the only choice.

item.title: Dan Wilson announces his own firing as Seattle Mariners manager in rare postgame moment
item.description: Dan Wilson broke MLB protocol by personally announcing his own dismissal as Seattle Mariners manager, delivering an emotional postgame address.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle Mariners manager Dan Wilson personally broke the news to his team and the media Sunday that he will not return for the 2027 season.

Before Game 162 against the Los Angeles Angels, Wilson held a closed-door meeting to inform players and staff.

Postgame, he stepped to the podium to deliver the news publicly and face questions before front-office executives addressed reporters.

Standard MLB protocol calls for front-office executives to issue a news release or hold a solo news conference while the ousted manager stays out of sight.

A manager taking the microphone to announce his own dismissal is virtually unheard of in modern sports.

"This season has been very difficult, and of course, the results have not been what any of us have expected," Wilson said. "As a result, it's concluded that today is my last day as manager of the Seattle Mariners."

Wilson, a former Mariners catcher who took over as manager in August 2024, acknowledged his deep roots in the organization.

"I'm still processing this with my family, and it's a very difficult day," Wilson said. "We love this city. We love this community and we appreciate the organization for what it has meant to the family since coming here as a player in '94. We feel extremely blessed by all the opportunities we've been afforded."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Expectations were sky-high entering 2026.

Coming off a 2025 AL West title and reaching Game 7 of the ALCS, Seattle fell just one win short of the World Series. Instead, the club collapsed to a 76-86 third-place finish.

The downward spiral was driven by offensive regression among core players, inconsistent starting pitching, a second-half bullpen collapse and some of the worst defensive metrics in Major League Baseball.

Late-season comments from players highlighted a lack of clubhouse accountability as a core failure. Pressed on whether leadership failed to enforce standards, Wilson faced the criticism directly.

"That's always a necessary component, and I think accountability comes in a lot of different ways," Wilson said. "Obviously, I think you look back, and there's a lot of things that you can point to, and perhaps that's one of them."

When asked if the front office made the final decision, Wilson accepted the reality of sports leadership.

"I've been in baseball a while, and this is what happens," Wilson said. "Managers shoulder the blame and shoulder the responsibility. And this is obviously difficult."

RED SOX REMOVE INTERIM TAG FROM MANAGER CHAD TRACY AFTER THE TEAM'S REMARKABLE SUMMER TURNAROUND

Seattle Mariners President of Baseball Operations Jerry Dipoto and General Manager Justin Hollander will return in 2027.

Dipoto noted that "collectively we failed to meet our own expectations" and agreed a leadership change was necessary.

Wilson finishes his tenure as Mariners manager with a 187-171 career record.

item.title: Trump CMS faces bipartisan pushback over Medicare proposal tied to Biden-era drug pricing law
item.description: Lawmakers say the proposed Medicare policy could make it harder for patients to access newer cancer treatments by discouraging medical innovation.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: A bipartisan group of more than 50 lawmakers is urging the Trump administration not to finalize a proposed Medicare policy tied to the Biden-era drug price negotiation program, arguing it could discourage development of improved cancer treatments.

In a Sept. 21 letter obtained by Fox News Digital, the lawmakers called on Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz to remove the agency's proposed fixed-dose combination policy from its final rule implementing Medicare's Drug Price Negotiation Program.

The Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program was created under the Inflation Reduction Act, which former President Joe Biden signed into law in 2022. The Trump administration proposed the policy in June as part of implementing that program.

At the center of the dispute is how Medicare would treat newer versions of existing drugs for price negotiation purposes.

DR OZ WARNS MEDICARE SCAMMERS ARE STEALING BILLIONS — AND YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION COULD BE NEXT

The lawmakers argue the proposal would cause some improved treatments to face Medicare price negotiations much sooner after receiving Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval. 

They say that would reduce incentives for drugmakers to develop better versions of existing medicines.

"If finalized, the proposed fixed-dose combination policy would subject these advancements to negotiation almost immediately after FDA approval, harming patient access as well as incentives to develop these improved therapies," the lawmakers wrote.

CMS, meanwhile, said the proposal is designed to prevent drugmakers from avoiding or delaying negotiated Medicare prices by making only limited changes to existing drugs and introducing them as new products.

DR OZ NAMES 5 STATES IN FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS MEDICAID ABUSE

The lawmakers pointed to advances in cancer immunotherapy that allow some patients to receive a quick injection instead of spending hours receiving an intravenous infusion. 

They said those improvements can make treatment faster, easier and more accessible, particularly for patients in rural areas.

"Patients fighting cancer deserve access to the most advanced new therapies, and if CMS finalizes this proposal, those advances are less likely to reach those who need it the most," the letter states.

The lawmakers also argued the FDA already evaluates the therapies as separate medicines, requiring separate clinical trials and approvals.

They said CMS should treat those therapies as separate medicines under the Medicare drug price negotiation program.

The lawmakers also argued that CMS actuaries "have not been able to show this policy would produce meaningful savings for taxpayers."

DR OZ REVEALS THE HEALTHY RETIREMENT HABIT THAT COULD MAKE AMERICA $1 TRILLION RICHER

"We strongly urge CMS to withdraw the fixed-dose combination proposal from the final rule," the letter states. "The patients we represent need policies that expand access to lifesaving care and reward medical progress and innovation in the treatment of deadly diseases."

The letter was signed by more than 50 lawmakers from both parties, including Reps. John Joyce, R-Pa., Darin LaHood, R-Ill., Mike Kennedy, R-Utah, Tim Moore, R-N.C., Jim Costa, D-Calif., Donald Davis, D-N.C., and more.

CMS could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

item.title: Grandmother sues after alleged AI facial recognition error led to months in jail, experts sound alarm
item.description: Angela Lipps was arrested at gunpoint and jailed for nearly six months after Fargo police allegedly relied on an uncorroborated AI facial recognition match.
item.content:encoded:
A Tennessee grandmother has filed a lawsuit against a North Dakota city and police department, accusing officials of wrongfully detaining her for nearly six months after allegedly misusing artificial intelligence facial recognition technology to investigate a bank theft case.

Angela Lipps, now 50, of Elizabethton, Tennessee, said she was caring for her neighbor's four young children when police showed up at the home and arrested her at gunpoint in July 2025.

The complaint, filed Sept. 15, 2026, alleges that authorities relied exclusively on a flawed AI facial recognition match to extradite Lipps from Tennessee to North Dakota, despite her having no connection to the crime or the state.

Experts on police technology told Fox News Digital that the case is among more than a dozen known instances involving alleged police mishandling of facial recognition technology.

"I sat in a county jail in Tennessee for 108 days," Lipps said in a GoFundMe post. "They said I was fugitive from justice. I had no bail. No one interviewed me. I just sat and waited."

FRAUD EXPERT WARNS AI IS HELPING CRIMINALS OUTPACE THE GOVERNMENT: 'DON'T HAVE THE RIGHT TOOLS'

The bank theft case stemmed from April and May 2025, when an unknown woman allegedly used fake IDs and stolen identities to perpetrate bank fraud in Fargo and West Fargo, North Dakota, according to the lawsuit.

Officials then used a photo from a fraudulent ID card presented by the suspect, rather than surveillance footage, to conduct facial recognition searches using Clearview AI, prosecutors alleged.

While Clearview AI explicitly requires facial recognition matches to be treated as potential leads, Fargo police allegedly characterized the AI match as a positive identification without disclosing that it had not been independently corroborated, according to the complaint.

Meanwhile, the West Fargo Police Department reportedly declined to seek charges because the AI match was uncorroborated.

A West Fargo police captain reportedly characterized AI facial recognition as "close to a last-ditch effort" in police investigations, the lawsuit said.

FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES

According to the complaint, Detective Lucas Heck did not review Lipps’ financial or travel records that showed she was in Tennessee during the bank thefts and failed to conduct photo lineups with bank tellers. Surveillance video reportedly showed physical differences between Lipps and the suspect, including a different build and a neck tattoo on Lipps that was absent from the suspect.

"Heck ignored, concealed, and misrepresented exculpatory evidence that Lipps did not commit the bank thefts," the complaint alleged.

On July 14, 2025, U.S. Marshals surrounded a neighbor’s house in Tennessee and arrested Lipps at gunpoint on a nationwide warrant, prosecutors said.

Lipps was extradited to North Dakota and reportedly held on a $100,000 bond while facing eight felony counts, the most severe of which carried maximum sentences of up to 10 years in prison.

Prosecutors dismissed all charges on Dec. 24, 2025, after Lipps produced bank records showing that she was in Tennessee when the bank thefts occurred, prosecutors said.

"When she was released, she found that her residence, car, and personal property were lost while she was absent," the complaint said.

FLOCK SAFETY CEO CALLS FOR NATIONAL 'COMPROMISE' AMID CAMERA SABOTAGE AND PUBLIC REVOLT

Following public scrutiny, the Fargo Police Department and city of Fargo acknowledged at a March 2026 press conference that the department had made investigative errors.

"When chief found some errors that were made in this area of where we got our facial recognition and how that worked, we immediately addressed it," Mayor Tim Mahoney said.

Clare Garvie, the deputy director of Technology Law & Policy with the Policing Project, told Fox News Digital that incidents involving the alleged mishandling of AI have increased as law enforcement agencies adjust to "integrate AI and additional tools into police investigations."

"We are aware of 16 misidentifications stemming from a face recognition match where someone was wrongfully arrested and spent time in jail because of that misidentification, and in many of these cases, it was because additional investigative steps weren't taken to prove, or in these cases to disprove, the face recognition match," Garvie said in an interview.

"We're asking officers to do a different job now, such that we need to update how we think about these workflows," she added.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Nate Freed-Wessler, a deputy director at the American Civil Liberties Union, said the rise of artificial intelligence in law enforcement has fueled wrongful arrests across the country.

"We've been seeing these kinds of wrongful arrests happening for at least five or six years now out of this kind of AI technology. And the rate of them seems to be increasing," he said.

"We've seen cases where police intentionally avoid making any notes about their use of facial recognition technology or other AI."

item.title: Former Obama aides claim Democratic donors are still holding back after being burned by 2024 loss
item.description: "Pod Save America" hosts say Democratic donors are holding back despite what they call a generational midterm election opportunity for the party.
item.content:encoded:
Former Obama advisers who host the "Pod Save America" podcast spoke Friday about the purported reasons some major Democratic donors are holding back money as the party sees encouraging signs ahead in November's midterm elections.

At the Texas Tribune Festival last week, the podcast hosts shared their optimism over Texas turning blue because of Republican struggles in purple states. Dan Pfeiffer spoke about numerous factors working against Republicans, even in rural areas, but still warned that Democrats have far less money to work with, compared to the GOP.

Tommy Vietor replied, "I think those spending restraints compared to the opportunity are why you're starting to hear some, you know, sort of operatives and candidates like voicing concern and frustration that some of the traditional like big, big donors of the Democratic Party, are not viewing this as the generational opportunity that it could be."

THE SOROS POLITICAL MACHINE IS PUTTING MILLIONS TO WORK BEFORE ELECTION DAY — AND ZEROING IN ON KEY RACES

"Because I was talking to someone today who was like, ‘Let me paint for you the like extreme optimistic picture,’ which is Democrats are not only winning on the generic ballot, but if you look at the top like most salient issues, we are crushing in those areas as well, which was not the case in 2024, right?," he continued.

Vietor proposed that if the results of this midterm election resemble recent special elections where Democrats overperformed, "it is like truly a historic opportunity to win statewide races, congressional races, down-ballot, up and down. And it just feels like a moment when all the biggest donors in the party should be pushing all their chips in the table as aggressively as possible and not holding back for — I don't know what reason — Trump bothering them?"

"Yeah, I think there has been a huge shift in the funding approach ... in the large donor community since 2024," Pfeiffer said. "Part of it is people still angry about how that election went and feeling like they lit a billion dollars on fire in that election, which is a fair quibble in some ways." 

"There are a lot of people who are very afraid of being targeted by Trump like that just that your business is going to be targeted," he continued. "You're going to have all of a sudden, you're going to the FBI is going to show up at your door. You're going to have regulatory scrutiny you wouldn't have before. And so that has limited money."

CASH-STRAPPED DNC SHELLED OUT MORE THAN $800K TO NON-VOTING TERRITORIES LIKE VIRGIN ISLANDS WHILE IN DEBT

Pfeiffer argued further that this midterm election could possibly lead to a scenario where "you're looking at one of the largest swings in American history, something where Democrats could pick up races we've never even thought possible," he said. "We've been using 2006 as like the most relevant example of an election because it's you know, it's an unpopular president, unpopular war, all of that. But it very well could be a little more like '94, where everything changes where it's a realigning election."

Democratic consultant Julian Epstein rejected the podcasters' comments.

"It's always funny to me how these group think 'insiders' parrot one another, even when they're 'consensus' is obviously wrong. The truth is that the so-called 'blue tsunami' is very likely overstated. The margin of error and the 40 battleground congressional districts is more like 2% right now, and we've consistently seen Republicans being undersampled in recent years," he told Fox News Digital.

"Donors are holding back because the Democrats don't have any attractive, positive agenda," he continued. "Democrats have an even lower approval rating than the president. Democrats used to be about building; today they are about tax-and-spend redistributionist big government welfare. They are about the victim Olympics."

"Try going out on the street and ask 10 voters to name three things Democrats stand [for] today. I doubt you'll find any that can," Epstein added.

Republican consultant Mary Marslender suggested the podcasters may have a key point.

"Yes, major Democratic donors are holding back, still frustrated by the fallout from the 2024 cycle and increasingly concerned about the party's direction," Marslender told Fox News Digital.

"Kamala Harris’ failed presidential campaign spent a staggering $1.5 billion in just 15 weeks, losing the popular vote, the Electoral College, the Senate, the White female vote, and support among both Latino and working-class voters," she continued. "That’s the equivalent of spending $25,000 per hour only to lose nearly every key demographic and benchmark the campaign touted as strengths."

"Major donors who contributed eight-figure sums in 2024 have noticed this poor return on investment and appear less willing to spend this cycle," she said.

"Additionally, many major Democratic donors have slowed or withheld contributions because of concerns about the Party’s shift toward socialist policies," Marslender added. "Unsurprisingly, calls to destroy the country’s financial institutions have not resonated well with wealthy Democratic supporters."

item.title: Sudden cruise itinerary change leaves some travelers upset, others celebrating 'gigantic win'
item.description: Royal Caribbean's Icon of the Seas' Costa Maya cruise stop was suddenly canceled after maintenance delays in Miami. Some passengers were disappointed as others applauded.
item.content:encoded:
Royal Caribbean's cancellation of an Icon of the Seas stop left some cruise passengers hugely disappointed and others wildly celebrating — sparking a debate over whether the port was worth visiting at all.

The stop — Costa Maya, a cruise port on Mexico's Caribbean coast — was scrapped from Icon of the Seas' Sept. 26 itinerary after a maintenance issue apparently kept the ship in Miami overnight.

The vessel was scheduled to depart Miami on Saturday but remained in port until Sunday, according to a Royal Caribbean notice sent to passengers as reported by Parade magazine.

BELOVED CRUISE SPOT WILL BE OFF LIMITS THROUGH 2027 AS SAFETY CONCERNS LINGER

A copy of the notice shared on Reddit said the ship would depart Miami on Sunday, Sept. 27, instead of Saturday, Sept. 26. "Day 3 will now be a relaxing Sea Day in place of our visit to Costa Maya, Mexico," the notice said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Royal Caribbean Group for comment.

The Reddit user who shared the news added that passengers were being offered at least $300 in onboard credit as compensation — with the amount varying by cabin type.

In response, many Reddit users surprisingly applauded the change.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Just got this. $350 to miss the worst port of the itinerary made my day!" one Redditor said. "Might go to the Supper Club with that, lol."

Wrote another person, "Three hundred dollar credit, and you don't have to go to Costa Maya? That's a gigantic win."

The strong reaction to the Costa Maya stop prompted questions from other travelers.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Other passengers, however, were disappointed about missing planned excursions to see the ancient ruins at Chacchoben, a Maya archaeological site near the port.

Another said, "I’m bummed to be missing our Chacchoben ruins tour, but we’ll live."

item.title: Dem Senate nominee breaks silence after Susan Collins' office was vandalized with vulgar message
item.description: Republican Sen. Susan Collins vowed she won't be "intimidated" after her Biddeford office was vandalized, while her Dem rival Troy Jackson initially stayed silent.
item.content:encoded:
Republican Sen. Susan Collins said she would not be "intimidated" after one of her Maine constituent offices was vandalized Monday, prompting her Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, to break his silence Monday night and condemn the "vandalism and intimidation" as "wrong."

The senator’s constituent office in Biddeford, Maine was vandalized on Monday, with the words "Trump Whore" sprayed on the entry doors. The senator’s office confirmed the incident, while a photo of the defaced doors was posted on Facebook and X by Maine state Sen. Matt Harrington, the assistant Republican leader in the chamber. Meanwhile, the Biddeford police confirmed the presence of an investigation into the matter to Fox News Digital.

"Vandalism is unacceptable. Senator Collins and her staff will not be intimidated. Our Biddeford constituent service office remains open, and we will continue serving the people of Maine," Collins Chief of Staff Katie Brown said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

SUSAN COLLINS DEFIES BLUE-STATE HEADWINDS IN CRUCIAL SENATE BATTLE AS NEW POLL REVEALS STRIKING SPLIT

Collins is running for re-election this year for a sixth six-year term representing blue-leaning Maine in the Senate, and is locked in a competitive contest with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson, the former Maine Senate president. The race is a must-flip for the Democrats as they try to recapture the Senate majority from the GOP in this autumn’s midterm elections.

"There’s no place for this in Maine. Vandalism and intimidation are wrong, full stop," Jackson told Fox News Digital after publication. "Senator Collins and her staff should be able to do their jobs without anyone defacing their office, and I condemn whoever did this."

SUSAN COLLINS DROPS BRUTAL REMINDER OF DEM RIVAL ROCKED BY ACCUSATIONS

Former Maine state Rep. Austin Theriault, the 2024 Republican congressional nominee who narrowly lost to Rep. Jared Golden, D-Maine, and is now seeking to return to the state House, told Fox News Digital "there shouldn't be any hesitation to condemn these sort of actions, regardless of where you are on the political spectrum."

"I'm very confident that Sen. Collins herself would very quickly condemn this if the shoe was on the other foot," Theriault said, while questioning whether Maine Democrats have an "identity problem" following Jackson's initial silence.

Maine GOP Communications Director Kristina Parker argued in a statement to Fox News Digital that the vandalism "is just another example of the radical left's aggression and inability to have civil discourse."

MAINE ICE SHOOTING VICTIM WAS NOT TARGET OF ARREST WARRANT, SEN. KING'S OFFICE SAYS AFTER EARLIER DHS ACCOUNT 

"We hope the prosecution is quick and smooth. Our political environment should not tolerate this volatile and disgusting behavior," she added.

Collins' office in Biddeford is located just a few blocks from the site of a fatal shooting by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in July. Following the shooting, protesters marched to the senator’s Biddeford office to demonstrate against Collins’ support for ICE funding.

The senator, a moderate Republican who has occasionally broken with President Donald Trump, has drawn bipartisan attention throughout the campaign. 

She received praise this summer after casting her 10,000th consecutive Senate vote, but has also faced criticism from both parties. Collins has criticized Trump's tariff policies toward Canada and voted against Attorney General Todd Blanche's confirmation, while Democrats have continued to target her over her defense of her 2018 vote to confirm Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, who later joined the Supreme Court majority that overturned Roe v. Wade.

item.title: Texas Longhorns Colin Simmons' vulgar sack celebration was inexcusable for a Christian athlete
item.description: Colin Simmons' vulgar sack celebration against Tennessee sparked backlash, raising questions about his faith after once bringing a Bible onto the field.
item.content:encoded:
Texas Longhorn defensive end Colin Simmons is arguably the best d-end in college football. He looks like a man among boys in the way he manhandles offensive tackles and sacks quarterbacks, but his antics in the Longhorns thrilling victory over Tennessee on Saturday showcased why he's still very much a boy in maturity.

Simmons, who claims to be a Christian, used to be best known for what he did following winning the Texas 6A Division I state championship with Duncanville High School. He brought a Bible onto the field and boldly proclaimed, "It ain't nobody but God!" In the biggest moment of his high school career, he pointed people to God. He deferred the glory, honor, and praise from himself and gave it to his Creator. It was refreshing to witness, just like it is every time we hear a player or coach do in their brightest moments. Now, Simmons is unfortunately known for one of college football's most vulgar sack celebrations ever.

Following a clutch third down sack, deep in the Tennessee side of the field, Simmons simulated pulling his penis out and peeing on the field. It wasn't just immature; it was utterly disgusting. Kirk Herbstreit called it "idiotic" on the broadcast and Chris Fowler, also calling the game, said it "it doesn't much [more] vulgar" than what Simmons did.

TEXAS DROPPED SOME CELEBRATIONS AGAINST TENNESSEE THAT WERE ABOUT AS UNHINGED AS THEY COME

What Simmons did wasn't just wrong as an athlete in a public setting. He was representing much more than just the Longhorns on national television, as a professing Christian, he's always representing Jesus Christ and the faith as a whole. No, thankfully the Christian faith isn't based on the moral failings of Simmons and I, but what we say and do are undoubtedly a reflection of our faith. That makes what he did much worse, in my opinion. No, that's also not to say an atheist athlete should be able to get away with this and shouldn't have to apologize. I'm simply stating that Christians, like myself, are held to the highest moral and ethical standards.

That's why I believe Trinindad Chambliss dropping an f-bomb in the postgame interview following Ole Miss' upset win over LSU, where he spent much of the interview praising God, was a bad look as well and worth apologizing over. It's unbecoming of a Jesus follower and showcased a blatant hypocrisy and major lack of control and discernment.

SAM ACHO Q&A: FORMER NFL PLAYER AND ESPN ANALYST SPEAKS OUT ON CIVILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN SPORTS AND MEDIA

Chambliss ended up apologizing postgame while wearing a "Jesus Won" T-shirt, showing true remorse for allowing the heat of the moment to cause himself to be a poor reflection of his faith saying, ""That’s not who I am. I’m deeply, deeply apologetic to Holly Rowe & everyone who was listening."

Houston Texans QB CJ Stroud addressed the problem with Christians cussing in an interview with Sports Spectrum in 2024. He said, "I can't proclaim I love God and have a wild mouth… it's hypocritical." He said this while references James 3, a biblical chapter focusing on the power and discipline of taming the tongue.

BUCS' EMEKA EGBUKA, WHOSE INSTAGRAM NAME IS 'CHRIST FOLLOWER,' EXPLAINS HOW FAITH HELPS DRIVE HIS CAREER

But what Simmons did was something that was incredibly difficult to imagine a professing Christian athlete ever doing. We all have trouble taming our tongue. I know I've had trouble with that over the years playing sports, and in times of frustration, but having a premeditated sack celebration with that level of vulgarity is inexcusable.

Simmons did apologize postgame, but saying you're remorseful and actually being remorseful are two very different things. Seemingly excusing his actions, Simmons stated, "I was definitely in that mode, feeling myself. It happens." That's not a valid excuse, in my opinion. It portrays a lack of understanding of the severity of his suggestive actions, especially as a Christian. Cussing happens. Losing our patience happens. Pretending to whip out your penis and pee on an opposing team's field doesn't just happen. That is a premeditated, unsportsmanlike, vulgar action that makes him look like a degenerate.

NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM

In the Bible, 1 Peter 4 addresses the Christians of the early church, who are called, just as Christians of this day and age, to hold themselves to a higher standard than they once did when they weren't Christians. As believers, we are to pursue holiness and encourage each other to pursue it, too.

That is why I'm calling my professed brother in Christ, Colin Simmons, to hold himself to that standard. I'm calling his Christian teammates, family members, coaches, and more, to help hold him accountable. Lord knows I need accountability too. Proverbs 17:7 says, "As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another." We can't do this Christian walk alone, and when money, status, and fame cause us to stumble, and lose sight of who we are, we need others to call us to repentance and get back on the straight and narrow pathway.

CLEVELAND BROWNS PLAYERS PUBLICLY BAPTIZED AT CLEVELAND FOR CHRIST EVENT IN POWERFUL DISPLAY OF FAITH

Christians have a moral framework from which we draw and are expected to live out. The unbelieving world and other Christians don't expect us to be perfect, but they certainly have every right to call us out on hypocrisy. I believe there is a moral standard embedded in every human and society, giving us an innate understanding of right and wrong to an extent, but there's no question whether actions like this by Simmons are wrong. It has no place in football. That's for sure.

Simmons tweeted after the game, "All Glory To God 🙏🏾 Thank you for listening to my prayers and forgive me for my actions."

LOUISIANA FOOTBALL PHENOM PEYTON HOUSTON CREDITS FAITH, FAMILY FOR HIS REMARKABLE SUCCESS

Here was my reply to him:

"This is a great learning experience, Colin. You have a lot of eye balls on you. Please use the platform & abilities God has given to be a good representation of Him. Don’t be like the world. Live like a man renewed through Christ. Thank God for His grace & forgiveness."

Let this be a message to all Christians, not just athletes with a platform playing on national television:
